changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers, replace the study claim with an offer: 'Send us one month of your statements and we'll show you what manual matching costs you, in your numbers.' Make this a standard SE motion. The SE builds the cost of manual matching from the customer's own statements and staff costs.
changes.why: The deal turned when the cost was built from one month of the controller's statements and the CFO claimed it with 'that's my number, not yours.', which a generic third-party study cannot do.

changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance buyers, especially a new CFO or a team with a long month-end close, lead the first call with: 'Know where your money is. Every deposit matched to its transactions and invoices in your ERP, without the spreadsheets.' Pair it with a discovery question on how long month-end close takes and who does the matching.
changes.why: Payout reconciliation was the only message that drew a reaction ('go back'), and the buyer described her problem as 'I just want to know where my money is.' and said 'the deposits', not payments.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers without engineers building anything, stop opening with M1, and drop M2 ('Built for developers') from the opener as well. Keep 'infrastructure' and 'payments' out of the headline for this audience. Open with the reconciliation line above instead.
changes.why: The standard deck's 'Financial infrastructure, global growth, all the currencies' got silence from a team that 'aren't building anything', and 'Nobody said 'infrastructure.'' on the customer side.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: Add a wholesale or distributor customer story (invoice-based B2B) and a reference contact who will take a call, for distributor and wholesale prospects.
changes.why: The buyer asked for a peer in 'Wholesale, invoices, that kind of business', rejected a story because 'this is a company that sells sweaters.', and raised the missing reference twice.
